svg.title: Protect Removal Cash Before Expanding Inventory
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Protect Removal Cash Before Expanding Inventory; subtitle: Four allocation buckets across $25,000, $100,000, and $200,000; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values show the $100,000 reference budget in USD. Each stage also provides its allocation at the canonical $25,000 minimum and $200,000 maximum. The allocation percentages are illustrative and sum to 100% at every capital level. Startup deployment is not annual revenue or annual expense.; caption: Minimum: $15,000 + $3,750 + $2,500 + $3,750 = $25,000. Reference: $60,000 + $15,000 + $10,000 + $15,000 = $100,000. Maximum: $120,000 + $30,000 + $20,000 + $30,000 = $200,000.; stages: label: Acquisition working capital; value: 60%; $60,000 reference allocation; numeric value: 60000.0; detail: Allocate $15,000 at minimum capital and $120,000 at maximum capital. Cover hammer prices, premiums, and acquisition cash obligations while limiting concentration in any single lot or buyer segment.; label: Removal and repair float; value: 15%; $15,000 reference allocation; numeric value: 15000.0; detail: Allocate $3,750 at minimum capital and $30,000 at maximum capital. Ring-fence loading, freight, inspection, testing, and bounded repair payments that fall due before resale collections.; label: Facilities and operating setup; value: 10%; $10,000 reference allocation; numeric value: 10000.0; detail: Allocate $2,500 at minimum capital and $20,000 at maximum capital. Fund appropriately scaled storage deposits, insurance setup, safety equipment, inventory controls, and required business registrations.; label: Liquidity and holding reserve; value: 15%; $15,000 reference allocation; numeric value: 15000.0; detail: Allocate $3,750 at minimum capital and $30,000 at maximum capital. Preserve cash for delayed collections, additional storage, and operating disruptions; calculate runway from actual monthly burn rather than assuming six months are funded.
